Michael States, Sharveshwaran Umashankar, Minsen Yuan, and Yue Yu
Abstract— Target tracking is the problem of estimating the
state of a target system using measurements collected (often-
times) by mobile sensors. Trajectory optimization for mobile
sensors must account not only for dynamical and operational
constraints, but also for uncertainty in estimating the target
system’s state. We propose an estimation-aware optimal control
method for target tracking that accounts for the nonlinear
dynamics of both the mobile sensor and target system, the
nonlinear covariance dynamics in extended Kalman filtering,
and nonlinear measurement models. Furthermore, it ensures
constraints on the mobile sensor are satisfied in continuous
time (within numerical precision). In numerical simulations,
the proposed method achieves estimation-aware target tracking
while satisfying the mobile-sensor constraints in continuous
time, even under sparse time discretization.
I. INTRODUCTION
Target tracking is the problem of estimating the state
of a dynamical target system using measurements. These
measurements are often collected bymobile sensors, which
are mobile platforms equipped with onboard sensing units
(such as aerial vehicles carrying range or bearing sensors).
The measurements often depend jointly on the states of the
mobile sensor and the target system. As a result, planning
the mobile sensor’s trajectory must account for not only the
sensor’s dynamics and operational constraints, but also how
measurements collected along the trajectory affect estimation
of the target system’s state. Target tracking has a wide range
of applications including search and rescue, environmental
monitoring, surveillance, and site inspection [1]–[4].
Existing work on target tracking uses various metrics to
quantify how the mobile sensor’s trajectory affects target
state estimation. One class of metrics involves the observ-
ability Gramian, which characterizes how well measurements
collected along the mobile sensor’s trajectory can distinguish
different initial states of the target [5]–[8]. Variants of the ob-
servability Gramian instead focus on the distinguishability of
the target’s final state [9]. Another direction uses the Fisher
information matrix to quantify the amount of information
that measurements provide about the target state [10]–[14].
A widely used metric is the state-estimation error covari-
ance, which directly quantifies the uncertainty of the state
estimate [15]–[26]. Covariance-based metrics are particularly
attractive because widely used estimators, like the Kalman
filter, provide a covariance that accounts for process noise
and measurement noise. Some methods use these metrics

discrete-time [8], [15], [17]–[20], [26] or continuous-time
Kalman filters [21]–[25].
One limitation of existing target-tracking methods is that
they only constrain the mobile sensor state in discrete time.
Constraints, such as keep-out zones, are often safety critical
and must be satisfied at all times, but since informative sens-
ing often requires aggressive maneuvers that drive the state
close to constraint boundaries, constraint violations can occur
between discretization points. Existing methods impose such
constraints either through explicitly discrete-time formula-
tions [10], [16]–[20] or through direct transcription and
collocation of continuous-time models [9], [22], [24], [25].
Reducing violations between discretization or collocation
points generally requires dense time discretization, which
increases the size and computational cost of the resulting
trajectory optimization problem.
Addressing this limitation by enforcing continuous-time
constraints introduces an additional computational challenge
for target tracking. Recent continuous-time optimal control
methods ensure constraint satisfaction between discretization
points by differentiating the underlying continuous-time dy-
namics equation [27], [28]. In target tracking, this dynamics
equation not only introduces nonlinear coupling between the
mobile sensor’s state and target covariance, but also must
preserve the covariance matrix’s symmetric structure. Some
recent results have developed efficient backpropagation-
based methods for differentiating covariance dynamics for
discrete-time extended Kalman filtering [18]. However, to the

id: http://arxiv.org/abs/1908.09208v3
published: 2019-08-24T21:02:09Z
summary: We study in this paper the wellposedness of path-dependent multidimensional forward-backward stochastic differential equations (FBSDE). By path-dependent we mean that the coefficients of the forward-backward SDE at time t can depend on the whole path of the forward process up to time t. These kinds of forward-backward SDE appear when solving path-dependent stochastic control problem by means of variational calculus. At the heart of our analysis is the construction of a decoupling random field on the path space. We first prove the existence and the uniqueness of decoupling field on small time interval. Then by introducing the characteristic BSDE, we show that a global decoupling field can be constructed by patching local solutions together as long as the solution of the characteristic BSDE remains bounded. Finally, we show that the solution of a path-dependent forward-backward SDE is stable.

title: Continuous-Time Estimation-Aware Optimal Control of Mobile Sensors for Target Tracking

We propose an estimation-aware optimal control method for target tracking that accounts for the nonlinear dynamics of both the mobile sensor and target system, the nonlinear covariance dynamics in extended Kalman filtering, and nonlinear measurement models. title: Equilibrium states for the classical Lorenz attractor and sectional-hyperbolic attractors in higher dimensions
id: http://arxiv.org/abs/2209.10784v3
published: 2022-09-22T05:02:42Z
summary: It has long been conjectured that the classical Lorenz attractor supports a unique measure of maximal entropy. In this article, we give a positive answer to this conjecture and its higher-dimensional counterpart by considering the uniqueness of equilibrium states for Hölder continuous functions on a sectional-hyperbolic attractor $Λ$. We prove that in a $C^1$-open and dense family of vector fields (including the classical Lorenz attractor), if the point masses at singularities are not equilibrium states, then there exists a unique equilibrium state supported on $Λ$. In particular, there exists a unique measure of maximal entropy for the flow $X|_Λ$.

title: What attracts to attractors?
id: http://arxiv.org/abs/1907.08101v2
published: 2019-07-18T15:06:09Z
summary: Whether, how, and to what extent solutions of Bjorken-expanding systems become insensitive to aspects of their initial conditions is of importance for heavy-ion collisions. Here we study 1+1D and phenomenologically relevant boost-invariant 3+1D systems in which initial conditions approach a universal attractor solution. In Israel-Stewart theory (IS) and kinetic theory where the universal attractor extends to arbitrarily early times, we show that all initial conditions approach the attractor at early times by a power-law while their approach is exponential at late times. In these theories, the physical mechanisms of hydrodynamization operational at late times do not drive the approach to the attractor at early times, and the early-time attractor is reached prior to hydrodynamization. In marked contrast, the attractor in strongly coupled systems is realized concurrent with hydrodynamization.
